confirmed_exposures.evidence: Executor.RunOne acquires the single session advisory lock before Reconcile, Claim, runtime acquisition, mutation, verification, and journal completion. Lifecycle verification can use a detached 45-second context after the nominal 30-second execution context.
confirmed_exposures.risk: One slow panel or verification can block all client mutations across workers and manual executors; the 5-second Drain budget is checked only between jobs and cannot bound one RunOne call.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: Panel-scoped classifyPanelFailure and recordPanelFailure are invoked only when isLifecycle(job.Payload). Equivalent manual or other non-lifecycle remote errors return from RunOne, terminate Drain, and cause main.go to call FailCloseGateWithFailure.
confirmed_exposures.risk: A remote failure attributable to one panel can stop unrelated panels and accounts.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: Unknown errors, SQL failures, and internal invariants are deliberately not panel-classified and propagate to global fail-close.
confirmed_exposures.risk: Large blast radius, but this is currently a deliberate safety policy rather than an accidental lifecycle bug.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: Claim decrements remaining_operations or remaining_batches before execution. runtimeUnavailable can decrement job attempts as a pre-mutation deferral, but recordPanelFailure does not refund the authorization budget. Auto-enrollment refuses existing scopes and exhausted budgets.
confirmed_exposures.risk: Repeated safe pre-mutation deferrals can exhaust finite authorization without performing the intended work; recovery requires explicit operator authorization.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: LifecycleWorker.Once processes up to 100 due items serially using the worker root context, with no per-item deadline in the supplied code.
confirmed_exposures.risk: One stalled provider or network call can delay all later expiry and deletion items and can leave heartbeat lifecycle progress stale.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: network.Monitor checks every proxy serially with an 8-second timeout and defaults all checks to api.ipify.org. The residential monitor also defaults to the same endpoint, although it uses bounded concurrency.
confirmed_exposures.risk: A large proxy set stretches observation age; endpoint or DNS failure can correlate health failures across otherwise independent proxies.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: ProcessLifecycle returns early when managedNow < desiredNow before reading the provider capacity snapshot and considering the oldest-expiring capacity-breaker path.
confirmed_exposures.risk: When the local desired deficit cannot be backfilled because provider occupancy is at its ceiling, an expiring resource may wait indefinitely instead of retiring to free a provider slot. The supplied logic is provider-neutral; an UpCloud-specific occurrence is not established here.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: RecoverDeployment selects unqualified next_retry_at from joined provision_step_attempts and provision_runs and ignores the Scan error.
confirmed_exposures.risk: Schema ambiguity or scan failure silently disables the intended retry deferral, allowing premature recovery attempts.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: Lifecycle, recovery, scheduling, client mutation, panel reconciliation, capacity, proxy monitoring, residential synchronization, and maintenance goroutines share one process and one 64-connection DB pool.
confirmed_exposures.risk: OOM, an unhandled panic, descriptor exhaustion, or process-wide stalls affect all worker subsystems. systemd Restart=on-failure helps only after process exit; WatchdogUSec=0 does not detect a live hang, and MemoryMax=infinity supplies no cgroup memory containment.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: Remote mutations and later journal completion are separate steps. A DB outage after remote success can prevent Succeed, verification persistence, and even durable global fail-close.
confirmed_exposures.risk: Writes cannot safely continue, and output cannot be declared globally verified until exact-scope reconciliation restores durable evidence.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: Client claims are globally ordered by created_at and id under one executor. Recovery dispatcher admission is bounded but rejected submissions are merely reconsidered on later scans; no explicit fair scheduler across accounts is shown.
confirmed_exposures.risk: Large or repeatedly retried workloads can increase tail latency for other accounts. Existing per-account recovery concurrency limits reduce domination but do not prove fairness.

confirmed_exposures.evidence: No supplied mechanism establishes memory limits, disk-space admission, watchdog-based stall recovery, clock-skew bounds, retry-storm control across all subsystems, or guaranteed replacement supply before expiry.
confirmed_exposures.risk: OOM, disk exhaustion, stalled progress, cascading retries, clock skew around expiry and retry timestamps, and replacement-supply deficits remain high-priority forecast scenarios.

existing_protections.evidence: Account, panel, inbound, client, kind, payload, and idempotency key are validated; conflicting reuse is rejected. Provider create recovery uses durable identities and adoption rather than ambiguous POST replay.
Unknown provider creates are reconciled by identity; deletes are treated as idempotent and reissued only after observation and mutation-generation checks.
Claims transactionally check global gates, exact panel/inbound scope, account and deployment state, inventory presence, lifecycle authorization, expiry, and panel health.
Known lifecycle remote failures are committed with panel health atomically; quarantine is sticky and claim paths do not bypass it.
Code intentionally does not refund operator budgets or automatically rearm existing scopes. This safety invariant must remain even if separate deferral accounting is introduced.
Recovery uses six global and two per-account lanes; several panel loops use semaphores; residential monitoring uses 16 workers; client mutation concurrency remains one.
Stale client runners are reconciled, operation and deployment state use lock versions or guarded transitions, and provider-confirmed deletion receipts are replayable.
Mutation paths check account network identity, mutation generation, provider/account state, authorization, and policy. No supplied code authorizes direct fallback when protected proxies are down.
API and worker use distinct 24 and 64 connection pools, preserving some PostgreSQL headroom, though worker subsystems still share one pool and process.
Worker heartbeat records recovery, scheduler, and lifecycle scan timestamps every ten seconds, enabling external stale-progress detection if such alerting exists.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Keep the global lock and gate until the exact job outcome is reconciled. Classify only provably panel-attributable remote failures into panel cooldown or quarantine; unknown, SQL, and invariant failures remain globally fail-closed.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Inject a 30-second mutation plus 45-second lifecycle verification on panel A; verify no second job starts while the lock is held, the measured Drain duration can exceed five seconds, and a known panel error blocks A without closing unrelated authorized panels.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Stop new writes, retain the RUNNING or unknown ledger state, restore DB availability, then perform exact panel/inbound/client observation before deciding success, retry, conflict, or quarantine. Never infer universal verification from process survival.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Fail DB commits immediately after a successful remote response; assert no duplicate ambiguous POST occurs and execution remains blocked until exact-scope reconciliation.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Pause protected mutations for affected routes, preserve pending durable intent, and require healthy authorized proxy evidence before resumption. Never fall back to direct egress.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Block the common test endpoint while proxy tunnels remain otherwise reachable; verify protected traffic does not use direct networking and endpoint correlation is distinguishable from proxy-specific failure.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Use fresh provider capacity evidence and an account-scoped single-retirement claim to decide whether the oldest expiring managed resource must retire before backfill. Do not increase general lifecycle concurrency.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Set managed below desired while provider in-use equals limit; verify exactly one eligible oldest expiring resource can enter retirement and later backfill, with no oversupply or duplicate retirement.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Use memory containment, external progress monitoring, and process separation for high-risk subsystems where justified. Recover only at narrow task boundaries with durable state cleanup; do not blanket-recover arbitrary panics.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Force memory pressure and a panic in a disposable subsystem; verify bounded host impact, systemd restart after exit, stale leases age out, and no mutation is replayed without reconciliation.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Fail closed for mutations, alert before critical reserve is exhausted, preserve audit and journal writes, and resume only after storage health and durable state are verified.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Exhaust a test volume during claim, remote execution, and completion phases; verify each phase yields a deterministic unknown or pending state and no output is falsely marked verified.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Add observable age and fair-share admission while retaining ownership leases and per-account limits. Apply scoped backoff and jitter rather than increasing blanket concurrency.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Load one account with thousands of retriable items and another with one due item; assert a bounded service-time objective for the second account and bounded retry rate per provider.

forecast_scenarios.safe_recovery: Prefer database time for durable eligibility, monitor host-to-DB skew, reserve explicit safety margins, and surface insufficient replacement supply rather than deleting or extending authorization implicitly.
forecast_scenarios.measurable_test: Skew worker time around scope expiry, next_retry_at, and droplet expiry; assert no expired authorization is consumed, no premature retry occurs, and unresolved replacement deficits become measurable stalled states.

priorities.action: Separate known panel-attributable remote failures from global internal failures for every client-mutation origin, while preserving global fail-close for SQL, unknown, and invariant errors.
Define DB-outage behavior and exact-scope reconciliation for remote-success/local-commit-failure cases.
Add external stale-progress supervision and memory containment; consider process separation for client mutations, lifecycle, and general recovery rather than shared-process expansion.
Correct the provider-ceiling versus desired-deficit decision ordering under the existing account-scoped retirement claim.
Bound lifecycle work per item and expose oldest-due age, without simply increasing concurrency.
Remove correlated proxy-health dependence through multiple controlled observation endpoints or endpoint-specific health classification; retain prohibition on direct fallback.
Fix and test the qualified retry-time query and error handling.
Add capacity planning and alerts for OOM, disk, DB connections, queue age/fairness, retry rate, clock skew, and expiry replacement deficit.

corrections.overclaim: The five-second Drain budget bounds mutation execution.
corrections.correction: It only prevents starting another iteration after the budget is observed; one RunOne can exceed it substantially.

corrections.overclaim: Panel isolation now covers remote client-mutation failures generally.
corrections.correction: The supplied panel failure path is restricted to lifecycle payloads; manual and other non-lifecycle jobs can still close the global gate.

corrections.overclaim: The capacity issue is proven UpCloud-specific.
corrections.correction: The ordering exposure is visible in provider-neutral lifecycle code. An UpCloud incident or provider-specific trigger is not demonstrated by the supplied source.

corrections.overclaim: Separate API and worker pools isolate worker subsystems.
corrections.correction: They isolate API pool pressure from worker pool pressure, but all worker goroutines share the same process and 64-connection pool.

corrections.overclaim: systemd restart and heartbeat provide hang recovery.
corrections.correction: Restart=on-failure handles process exit; WatchdogUSec=0 means systemd does not detect a live stalled process. Heartbeat data helps only if externally evaluated.

corrections.overclaim: Fresh provider observation makes all recovery outcomes authoritative.
corrections.correction: Authority is operation-specific. DB unavailability or a missing durable completion still requires exact-scope reconciliation and cannot justify declaring all output verified.

corrections.overclaim: The fixed per-panel lifecycle and stale UI races establish broad immunity.
corrections.correction: Those incidents are user-reported historical context. The supplied source confirms current backend boundaries only, contains no UI DOM source, and cannot establish exhaustive immunity or non-recurrence.

corrections.overclaim: The unqualified retry query is proven to fail in production.
corrections.correction: The unqualified column and ignored Scan error are confirmed code exposures; actual SQL ambiguity depends on the deployed schema, and no observed failure is supplied.

corrections.overclaim: Removing locks or increasing concurrency is the direct remedy.
corrections.correction: The locks preserve serialization and ownership invariants. Remediation should shorten or partition only provably safe critical sections and improve scoped isolation, reconciliation, fairness, and observability.

review_corrections_from_fresh_evidence: Deployed schema confirms next_retry_at exists in both joined provisioning tables, so the unqualified query is ambiguous; Scan errors are ignored.
Readiness evaluates recovery, scheduler and lifecycle scans; it does not establish client-mutation or Output collector progress.
Two old pending automatic jobs currently have expired scopes; this is stale-ledger evidence, not proof they are blocking current eligible claims.
No enabled unexpired scope is budget-exhausted in this sample.
Existing global mutation lock is an intentional safety boundary. Do not remove it or change concurrency without exact-scope locking, fenced durable recovery and fault/race acceptance.

target_acceptance: No new claim that all future failures can be predicted. Each failure must affect the smallest provably safe scope; healthy domains must make bounded progress. Unknown remote effects are observed before retry; shared DB failure blocks writes. Protected traffic never falls back directly. No auto-clear quarantine, budget reset or auth bypass.
